newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - Sept 14.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - Sept 14.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Bangladesh press on Saturday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

The Awami League government would seek advice from experts and talents in different fields in running the country, Commerce and Industries Minister Tofael Ahmed said. "Knowledgeable persons will be consulted in decision making," he said.
Opposition Bangladesh Nationalist Party has constituted a probe body to investigate last week's killing of 28 bengali-speaking woodcutters in Chittagong Hill Tracts by tribal insurgents.
The government would spend five billion taka ($125 million) in next five years to develop the country's riverine transport network, Shipping Minister A S M Abdur Rab said.

Police, under pressure from fans, will exhume on Saturday body of Bangladesh silverscreen super-star Salman Shah for a second autopsy after five days of his burial. Shah was found dead at his apartment on September 6, and doctors, after autopsy, said he had committed suicide.

Bangladesh Finance Minister S.A.M.S. Kibria said the country would resume stalled reforms for its own interest, and not because donors wanted it. "We have to carry on reforms for our own cause, what the donors say is immaterial", Kibria said on Friday on return from Aid Consortium meeting in Paris.
